summary: Vitamin D supplements reliably raise blood levels. How much is right depends on your starting level, body size and sun exposure, and very high doses can be harmful, so ask a pharmacist or doctor.
whyThisGrade: Consistent dose-response trials, reviewed by the Institute of Medicine
Raising the level is well shown; health benefits in people who aren't deficient are less clear

studies.title: The 2011 report on dietary reference intakes for calcium and vitamin D from the Institute of Medicine: what clinicians need to know
